stem: A propagation trainee selects a long stem section that contains no usable node at the intended cutting position. Which anatomical concept was overlooked?
choices: Nodes organize leaves, axillary structures, and potential growth points, so cutting selection should consider node placement rather than stem length alone
Internodes are the only tissues capable of forming shoots
Glandular trichomes determine whether a cutting can root
Leaf color identifies the correct cutting position
rationale: Node placement is operationally important in propagation. Total stem length does not substitute for identifying the structures needed for a repeatable cutting procedure.
